problem_restatements: Compute the landing point of a single evolution step of the shift dynamical system T_b(a) = (a+b) mod p, where the state space has period boundary p, for 9 distinct periodic regimes.
Decompose modular sum into free accumulation (s = a + b) followed by a piecewise period fold (s mod p = s - p * indicator(s >= p)). Since a+b < 2p, exactly one fold suffices.
analogy: Poincare return map on periodic state space. Orbits wrap at period boundary p. The return map subtracts p to fold the state back onto [0, p-1]. Modular addition decomposes into free evolution + single fold.

ops: orbit_state_initializer: Maps a, b to state vectors s_a=E_a[a], s_b=E_b[b] and prime to boundary vector beta=E_p[p_idx]
state_accumulator: s_free = s_a + s_b (element-wise, unbounded sum). Beta passes through unchanged.
poincare_return_map: crossing = dot(w_detect, s_free - beta) + b_detect; gate = sigmoid(crossing); s_folded = s_free - gate * beta. Differentiable piecewise fold.
orbit_readout: logits = W_out @ s_folded + b_out. Linear projection to class scores.
plan.reasoning: Mod has exact two-stage decomposition: linear accumulation + piecewise fold. Architecture makes this explicit. Boundary vector beta carries prime-specific period info. Single gated subtraction handles the wrap for all primes.

expected_outcome: Fast convergence (<500 epochs) to >95% accuracy with under 1000 params. Single learnable nonlinearity (gated fold) trains stably.
falsification: Fails if: (1) embeddings can't support additive compositionality, (2) sigmoid gate can't sharpen near boundary, (3) 9 boundaries interfere in shared state space.
look_back: Mathematically exact in the limit: if embed faithfully represents a+b and gate perfectly switches at boundary, computes mod without error.
Works for any modulus where a+b < 2*modulus, not just primes.
Structurally distinct from rotation (no periodicity), harmonic (no frequency domain), and syndrome (no iteration).
